# OmniGrid — The Outage With Three Versions of the Truth
> **GitHub-first narrative · GICS10 Utilities · 2026-10-19.** Fictional architecture learning case. GitHub is canonical; Notion is the KM hub. New people, incidents and options are illustrative. Original research and13HR child references remain below. Unattended synchronization is unverified.
**Start here:** [Executive One-Pager](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/executive-one-pager.md) · [Hero Story](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/hero-story.md) · [22-Section Master](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/README.md) · [16 Personas](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md) · [12 Simulations](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/simulations/README.md) · [Seven Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [Resources](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/resources/README.md)
## Prologue — A coordination gap
An invented storm exercise creates conflicting outage, asset and work-order status. Field and customer teams cannot reconcile next ownership. This prompts discovery, not a claim of an actual incident orproven cause.
## Act I — Understand the Enterprise (OGU-M01–04)
Fictional CEO **Anika Sørensen (OGU-P01)** leads a source-stipulated **USD31B** utility with **38,000staff,17countries and21M electricity/gas/water accounts**, headquartered in Copenhagen/Sydney. Accounts do not necessarily equal unique people.
Mix:renewables28%, networks27%, retail18%, conventional/flexible15%, water/environment12%.
Source explicitly identifies **Utilities/GICS10**, resolving the request's Communication Services wording.
[Enterprise theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/theme-a-enterprise.md)
## Act II — Choose the Future (OGU-M05–08)
Operations chief **Arjun Mehta (OGU-P04)** requires local authority; customer chief **Maya Patel (OGU-P03)** asks about affordability/participation; CFO **David Chen (OGU-P02)** challenges economics.
Compare local asset/region pilots, central platform/grid first and federated coordination experiments under common guardrails. Third option provisional.
Source99.99%reliability,30%faster restoration and15%capital-productivity improvement lack sufficient scope/baselines.
[Strategy theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/theme-b-strategy.md)
## Act III — Architect Trusted Coordination (OGU-M09–12)
Source chain: **Forecast → Generate → Transmit → Distribute → Consume → Flex → Restore**. It is electricity-centric; water/gas workflows require discovery.
**Mei Lin (OGU-P09)** and **Daniel Weber (OGU-P12)** connect Asset/Grid/Customer/Energy/WorkOrder360, ADMS/SCADA/EAM/OMS/CIS/billing/market systems and governed industrial/API/event contracts.
**Omar Haddad (OGU-P10)** requires permissions, segmentation, monitoring and recoverability. Source edge/hybrid/self-healing proposals are not validated operating controls.
[Architecture theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/theme-c-architecture.md)
## Act IV — Fund and Sequence Evidence (OGU-M13–16)
Source proposes **USD970M over3years** and **USD360M annual value**. Deferred capital, operating savings, loss reduction and flexible revenue need distinct cash/timing treatment. Split, run cost, overlap and discounting absent; NPV/payback unvalidated.
Year1 asset data, OT security, grid-data platform → Year2 ADMS, maintenance, field mobility → Year3 DER orchestration, self-healing pilots and customer flexibility.
Targets:95%critical records complete;20%faster restoration/15%fewer failures;30%flex participation/25%lower losses.
[Transformation theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/theme-d-transformation.md)
## Act V — Make Change Usable and Accountable (OGU-M17–19)
Field lead **Marcus Okoro (OGU-P08)** asks who owns the next work step. CHRO **Nadia Fernandes (OGU-P07)** requires role/shift practice and support.
Illustrative first pilot uses synthetic data and simulated events to test identifiers, topology freshness, permissions, late events, work ownership, reconciliation, offline behavior and rollback. No live grid, water orplant action executed.
[Execution theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/theme-e-execution.md)
## Act VI — Prove Community Value (OGU-M20–22)
SAIDI/SAIFI, restoration, curtailment, asset failures, losses, satisfaction and carbon measures require baselines, owners, cohorts and balancing measures.
**30%restoration ambition versus20%Year2target** remains a scope/time/definition gap. Completeness is not accuracy; carbon intensity is not absolute emissions. All future figures are targets, not results.
[Value theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/master/theme-f-value.md)
## Meet the Fictional Stakeholders
Anika Sørensen—CEO; David Chen—CFO; Maya Patel—Customer/Flexibility; Arjun Mehta—Operations; Elena Brooks—Generation; Sofia Tan—Digital; Nadia Fernandes—CHRO; Marcus Okoro—Outage/Field; Mei Lin—Asset/Grid Data; Omar Haddad—OT Security; Grace Menon—Water; Daniel Weber—EA; Priya Shah—Asset/Work Planning; Ravi Patel—Market/Energy; Amelia Jones—Community; Ingrid Sørensen—Procurement/Partners.
[Authority, objections and withheld evidence](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md)
## Practice and Derive
Twelve simulations cover discovery, outage coordination, funding, OT governance, data quality, skills, flexibility, customer experience, water scope, partners, architecture and hypothetical STAR.
Seven blueprints cover Workforce/HR, CX, Finance, Procurement, Asset/Field/Service Operations, Business Transformation and Leadership.
**13HR child links preserved**, with inline Workforce Monday summary; child bodies/implementations unaudited. External media remain planned.
[Scripts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/simulations/scenario-scripts.md) · [Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [13 HR references](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/references/notion-child-cases.md)
## Source and Synchronization Governance
Original research stays protected. Exact narrative maps to a GitHub baseline; conflicting edits are held. Other canonical changes need deliberate reconciliation; child pages and attachments are not losslessly mirrored.
[Sources/gaps](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/references/source-and-assumptions.md) · [Sync protocol](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/sync/README.md) · [Delivery report](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/10-utilities/omnigrid-utilities-ltd/delivery-report-2026-10-19.md)
**Delivery validation:** GitHub-to-Notion narrative was read back successfully. This note originated in Notion for the reverse-transfer test. OmniGrid is registered for daily reconciliation; unattended integration remains unverified.

# 🌟 GICS10. OmniGrid Utilities Ltd. — Business Transformation Case Study ## **Company Overview** **OmniGrid Utilities Ltd.** is a fictional multinational utilities company delivering electricity generation, transmission, distribution, renewable energy, water, and smart-energy services. It is transforming into a resilient, decarbonised, customer-centred energy system operator. --- ## **📊 Company Profile**
**Attribute** **Details**
**Founded** 1968
**Headquarters** Copenhagen, Denmark & Sydney, Australia
**Operating Markets** 17 countries
**Annual Revenue** \$31 billion USD
**Employees** 38,000 engineers, operators, and field teams
**Customers** 21 million electricity, gas, and water accounts
### **Business Portfolio**
**Segment** **Revenue %** **Operations**
Renewable Generation 28% Wind, solar, hydro, storage, green hydrogen
Networks & Distribution 27% Transmission, distribution, substations, smart meters
Retail Energy Services 18% Residential and business energy plans, demand response
Conventional & Flexible Generation 15% Gas, peaking capacity, balancing services
Water & Environmental Services 12% Water supply, treatment, wastewater, reuse
--- ## **🎯 Digital Transformation Vision** > *“Powering resilient, affordable, and low-carbon communities through intelligent grids, flexible energy, and trusted customer participation.”* ### **Transformation Drivers** 1. **Decarbonisation:** integrate growing renewable, storage, and distributed-energy resources. 2. **Grid Resilience:** prepare for extreme weather, cyber risk, and ageing infrastructure. 3. **Customer Participation:** enable flexible demand, prosumers, EVs, and transparent energy choices. 4. **Asset Productivity:** improve maintenance, reliability, and capital planning. 5. **Regulatory Performance:** provide auditable safety, reliability, affordability, and ESG reporting. --- # 🏗️ **TOGAF-Aligned Architecture Design** ## **Phase A: Architecture Vision** ### **Current-State Challenges** - Operational technology, field systems, customer platforms, and market data remain fragmented. - Variable renewable generation creates new forecasting and balancing complexity. - Asset inspections and outage restoration depend on manual processes and incomplete context. - Smart-meter and sensor growth expands cyber attack surface and data-management demands. ### **Stakeholder Outcomes**
**Stakeholder** **Outcome** **Success Measure**
Customers & Communities Reliable, affordable, transparent service 99.99% reliability and improved satisfaction
Regulators Safe, resilient, decarbonised infrastructure 100% compliant reliability and ESG reporting
Field Teams Safe, informed, efficient operations 30% faster outage restoration
Investors Disciplined transition and asset returns 15% better capital productivity
## **Phase B: Business Architecture** ```plain text UTILITY VALUE STREAM Forecast → Generate → Transmit → Distribute → Consume → Flex → Restore Future State: self-aware, flexible, resilient, low-carbon energy and water systems. ```
**Capability** **Target State** **Digital Enablers**
Grid Operations Predictive and self-healing ADMS, digital twin, real-time telemetry
Asset Management Condition-based and risk-informed IoT, drone inspection, predictive analytics
Customer Energy Services Personalised and participatory Smart-meter insights, demand-response platform
Outage Response Proactive and coordinated Event command centre, mobile workforce tools
## **Phase C: Information Systems Architecture** ### **Data Architecture** ```plain text UTILITIES GOLDEN RECORDS Asset 360° → Grid 360° → Customer 360° → Energy 360° → Work Order 360° ``` - **Operational data:** SCADA, AMI, weather, DER, network topology, reliability, and outage events. - **Asset data:** condition, maintenance history, criticality, risk, spares, and lifecycle cost. - **Customer data:** accounts, consent, consumption, service, billing, and flexibility preferences. - **Governance:** data lineage, safety controls, OT/IT security, regulatory retention, and trusted sustainability metrics. ### **Target Application Landscape**
**Layer** **Core Systems** **Pattern**
Experience Customer app, outage map, field mobility, partner portal Real-time and accessible journeys
Process ADMS, SCADA, EAM, OMS, CIS, billing, market systems Event-driven operational workflows
Integration Industrial gateway, iPaaS, event mesh, DER APIs Secure IT/OT interoperability
Data Utility lakehouse, historian, asset graph, ESG platform Streaming, governed data products
## **Phase D: Technology Architecture** - **Edge intelligence:** local processing for critical substations, plants, meters, and field operations. - **Hybrid cloud:** secure OT controls at the edge and private environments; scalable analytics and customer services in cloud. - **Zero trust for critical infrastructure:** network segmentation, hardened identity, continuous monitoring, and practiced incident response. --- # 🤖 **AI & Advanced Analytics**
**Use Case** **Business Value** **Approach**
Outage Prediction & Restoration Fewer and shorter interruptions Weather, topology, and asset-risk models
Renewable Forecasting Better balancing and lower curtailment Weather-informed time-series ML
Asset Health Management Lower failure and maintenance cost Sensor analytics and risk prioritisation
Energy Advisor Higher customer participation and savings Consent-aware personalised insights
--- # 📊 **3-Year Roadmap & Value Realisation**
**Phase** **Key Initiatives** **Success Metrics**
**Year 1 — Foundation** Asset-data quality, OT security uplift, smart-grid data platform 95% critical asset records complete
**Year 2 — Acceleration** ADMS rollout, predictive maintenance, digital field workforce 20% faster restoration; 15% fewer failures
**Year 3 — Transformation** DER orchestration, self-healing pilots, flexible customer services 30% flexible-load participation; 25% lower grid losses
### **Investment & Outcomes** - **3-year investment:** \$970M in grid modernisation, cyber resilience, data, field mobility, and distributed-energy platforms. - **Expected benefits:** \$360M annual value from improved reliability, deferred capital, lower loss, asset efficiency, and flexible-energy revenue. - **Core KPIs:** SAIDI/SAIFI, restoration time, renewable curtailment, asset failures, energy losses, customer satisfaction, and carbon intensity. --- # 🎉 **Conclusion** **OmniGrid Utilities Ltd.** evolves into an intelligent utility that protects reliability while accelerating the energy transition. Its transformation depends on secure IT/OT convergence, trusted asset and grid data, resilient operating models, and meaningful customer participation. --- ## 14. Aligned business transformation case study blueprint ## Alignment purpose This section refines OmniGrid into the same business transformation case study structure used for OmniSpace while preserving the existing content. ### 14.1 Executive case narrative OmniGrid Utilities Ltd. is transforming from traditional utility operations into a resilient, decarbonized, customer-participatory, intelligent grid and water-services ecosystem. **Core transformation statement:** OmniGrid is not only modernizing grid systems; it is building a governed transformation operating model where asset data, grid telemetry, customer participation, DER orchestration, OT security, resilience, ESG, and value realization work together. ### 14.2 Business problem statement
**Problem area** **Current challenge** **Transformation need**
Fragmented IT/OT landscape OT, field, customer, market, and asset systems are not fully integrated. Create Asset 360, Grid 360, Customer 360, Energy 360, and Work Order 360.
Renewable variability Wind, solar, storage, and DER growth make forecasting and balancing harder. Build renewable forecasting, DER orchestration, and flexibility platforms.
Reactive outage response Restoration depends on manual processes and incomplete field context. Deploy outage prediction, ADMS, OMS, and mobile workforce tools.
Asset risk and ageing infrastructure Maintenance and capital planning need better condition and risk intelligence. Use IoT, drone inspection, asset-health analytics, and risk-based planning.
Critical infrastructure cyber risk Smart meters, substations, sensors, and connected operations increase exposure. Apply zero trust, segmentation, OT monitoring, and incident-response readiness.
### 14.3 Target transformation operating model ```plain text Business Outcomes ↓ Capability Architecture — Grid, asset, customer energy, outage, market, ESG ↓ Process Architecture — Forecast, generate, transmit, distribute, consume, flex, restore ↓ Data Architecture — Asset, grid, customer, energy, work order golden records ↓ Application Architecture — ADMS, SCADA, EAM, OMS, CIS, billing, market systems ↓ Integration Architecture — Industrial gateway, iPaaS, event mesh, DER APIs ↓ Technology Architecture — Edge intelligence, hybrid cloud, AI, smart meters ↓ Cyber Resilience, Customer Participation, ESG, and Value Realization ``` **Operating rule:** Every utilities workstream must connect reliability, safety, asset data, grid telemetry, customer impact, regulatory control, cybersecurity, adoption, and measurable value. ### 14.4 Workstream alignment map
**Workstream** **Business outcome** **Architecture / process focus** **Delivery and adoption focus**
Grid modernization Higher reliability and better renewable integration. ADMS, SCADA, topology, telemetry, DER data. Smart-grid platform, forecasting, control-room adoption.
Asset health and field work Lower failures and faster restoration. Asset 360, EAM, OMS, work-order lifecycle. Predictive maintenance, drone inspection, field mobility.
Customer participation Flexible demand, prosumer engagement, and better satisfaction. Customer 360, smart-meter data, demand response. Energy advisor, customer app, flexibility programs.
Critical infrastructure resilience Secure, compliant, recoverable operations. OT security, identity, segmentation, regulatory controls. Monitoring, incident response, resilience exercises.
### 14.5 Case study structure for publishing 1. **Situation** - OmniGrid operates generation, networks, retail energy, flexible capacity, water, smart meters, and environmental services. 2. **Challenge** - It must improve reliability, decarbonize, integrate DERs, protect critical infrastructure, and engage customers. 3. **Transformation approach** - Use ADMS, grid digital twins, asset analytics, DER APIs, smart-meter insights, edge intelligence, and zero-trust OT security. 4. **Execution model** - Improve asset data, secure OT, deploy smart-grid platforms, modernize field work, and scale flexible-energy services. 5. **Value realization** - Measure SAIDI/SAIFI, restoration time, renewable curtailment, asset failures, grid losses, satisfaction, and carbon intensity. 6. **Long-term capability** - Build a repeatable utility transformation model for resilient, low-carbon, participatory energy and water systems. ### 14.6 Alignment rules - **Reliability first:** Digital change must improve safe, affordable, resilient service. - **Grid data as product:** Asset, topology, telemetry, and outage data must be governed. - **Secure IT/OT convergence:** Critical infrastructure needs segmentation and monitoring. - **Customer participation by design:** Prosumers, EVs, and demand response must be easy to join. - **Decarbonization embedded:** Carbon and flexibility metrics guide operating choices. - **Value after go-live:** Track operational and regulatory benefits continuously. ### 14.7 Final aligned positioning ## Aligned case study positioning OmniGrid Utilities Ltd. demonstrates how utility transformation becomes measurable when grid modernization, asset intelligence, DER orchestration, customer participation, OT cybersecurity, resilience, ESG, and value realization operate as one connected model.
